Subject: Post-demo: private deployment connectivity & performance acceptance pathways

Alex — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on what's needed to validate performance for a Private (VPC) deployment.

High-level acceptance asks we discussed:
- Tail/streaming latency: target p95 end-to-end < 150ms for streaming token delivery (prefer p95 < 120ms if possible).
- Concurrent sessions: sustained 150 concurrent streaming sessions with bursts to 400 for 10m windows.
- Throughput: baseline 250 TPS (inference requests/sec) across your initial pool; ability to scale to 600 TPS with Redwood Dedicated/Private autoscale.
- Egress/peering: peered VPC + IPSEC VPN fallback; NAT egress through ClearStream-managed gateways is acceptable if we can guarantee <25ms added egress overhead.

What we need from you to scope the private acceptance run:
1) Network path diagram (layered): which subnets, NAT/gateway IPs, and where peering/VPN will terminate.
2) Expected RTT/latency numbers between your application frontend and the planned peering endpoint (median + 95th).
3) Any egress devices (NAT gateways, firewalls) that will do deep packet inspection or TLS termination.
4) Load window and expected concurrency patterns (steady state + burst profile).

Attachments: I attached our recommended SLO matrix (redwood-slo-matrix.xlsx) with example test harness parameters. If you can send the network diagram and current egress IP ranges by EOD Friday PST, we’ll schedule a short handoff with the infra team to run a controlled smoke test next week.

Thanks —

Priyom — thanks for the clear recap. Looping in our NetOps alias; attaching our logical network diagram and a short note about our current egress topology.

Quick replies to your asks:
- Diagram attached: clearstream-net-diagram.pdf (high-level, includes VPN termination and NAT regions).
- RTTs: from our app layer (us-west-2) to the planned peering endpoint our monitoring shows median ~18ms, p95 ~42ms over TCP.
- Egress: traffic currently exits through two redundant NAT gateways (us-west-2a/b). No TLS termination on the gateway — TLS is end-to-end at the app. No DPI.
- Concurrency profile: steady 120 concurrent sessions during peak hour; synthetic bursts up to 420 for ~7 minutes during marketing events.

Notes / caveats:
- Our VPN uses IPsec (IKEv2) with a 1400 MTU to avoid fragmentation across third-party transit.
- We have a midstream load balancer that may add 4–8ms occasionally.

We'll plan to provide a list of egress IPs and a small NAT timing sample (tcpdump + timestamps) by Friday. If you need a temporary allowlist for a smoke window next week, let us know the IPs to expect from Redwood.

—Alex

Alex — appreciate the quick turnaround. A couple of technical clarifications from our infra team (cc'd: Aditya) so we can finalize the test plan: 

1) E2E measurement approach: we will run two parallel tests during the smoke window:
   - Streaming tail-latency: simulated streaming clients that open a long-lived websocket and measure token arrival p50/p95/p99. Target p95 < 150ms (goal 120ms).
   - Request/response throughput: short request payloads (<=256 tokens) measured at the load generator to validate 250 TPS baseline and burst capacity to 600 TPS for 10 minutes.

2) Network requirements we need from your side before the run:
   - Allowlist: Redwood will provide three public egress IPs for the test harness. Please allow those on your firewall for the 2hr window.
   - MTU: please confirm you can accept 1400 MTU on the peering/VPN path (IPsec overhead). If not, we'll adjust the test packetization.
   - Idle keepalive: please enable TCP keepalive (interval <= 60s) for the NICs handling the peering to avoid premature session drops during streaming.

3) Measurement gating: if the initial smoke shows p95 streaming > 220ms or packet loss > 0.5% we will stop and triage — those are hard cutoffs for this initial acceptance run.

Aditya — can you propose dates next week for a 90m window (preferred: Tue morning PST or Wed afternoon PST) and the exact Redwood egress IPs?

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
